- Model consistently underestimates prices in early days of the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes in recent history (e.g., after 88+ values), often overshooting by 2–5%.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting mean reversion is not captured.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly for downward trends.
- Model exhibits overconfidence in short-term volatility, leading to erratic swings in middle forecast days.
- When true price drops sharply, model fails to adjust downward quickly, often holding too high for 2–3 days.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price recovery after dips, especially in the 10–15 day window.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than actual price volatility, missing sudden reversals or spikes.
